A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original preprocessing Appendix C is retained as Appendix D in v6.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original geometric-image simulations, bird-classification experiments, and pneumonia-detection experiments, including classifier accuracies and estimated causal relationships.

after.justification: V6 retains those original empirical results and adds GRaSP-FCI experiments on the bird and X-ray datasets in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed macro-feature/PAG explanation framework, FCI procedure, and prediction models are retained. V6 expands the explanation of existing FCI steps and evaluates GRaSP-FCI as a sensitivity comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same geometric-image simulation, Caltech-UCSD bird data, and ChestX-ray8 subset. GRaSP-FCI reuses the existing datasets; the added annotation approaches are discussed without being evaluated.

E2.justification: V6 adds an evaluated comparison between FCI and GRaSP-FCI for both real-data experiments (Section 6.3 and Appendix C). The existing LIME and SHAP comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds a GRaSP-FCI experimental configuration using the BDeu score and chi-square independence tests, with other settings inherited from FCI. Existing data splits, predictor architectures, and real-data FCI thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix C tests whether causal-feature rankings depend on the PAG-learning algorithm. This adds a focused sensitivity analysis across both retained real-data tasks, alongside the existing bootstrap analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 50 bird-data bootstrap replicates and 100 X-ray replicates and report edge frequencies as stability measures. GRaSP-FCI uses the same reporting practice; no new seed, confidence-interval, or repeated-run reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 15 adds GRaSP-FCI edge-stability results: Crown Color and Size lead for birds, unlike the retained FCI leaders Wing Shape, Wing Pattern, and Tail Shape. X-ray feature ordering agrees across learners. Existing classifier accuracies and Figure 8 results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The structural assumptions, causal definitions, and Shapley calculations in Example 1 and Appendix A are retained. The expanded FCI description restates existing mathematics; the hybrid algorithm's correctness proof is cited rather than newly supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contribution: explaining black-box predictions through interpretable macro-features while distinguishing causal relationships from associations induced by unmeasured confounding.

C2.justification: Sections 4 and 7.3 add substantive qualifications about finite-sample conditional-independence errors and noisy annotations. V6 also discusses possible semi-supervised and LLM-assisted annotation and acknowledges differences between the learners' bird-feature rankings.

D1.justification: Appendix C documents the GRaSP-FCI implementation in TETRAD, its BDeu score, and reused settings. Appendix B removes the simulation's explicit significance level of 0.005, reducing reproducibility detail without establishing an actual setting change.

R1.justification: V6 adds references supporting hybrid discovery, causal representations, event-level explanation, annotation methods, and measurement-error limitations, including Lam, Schölkopf, Beckers, Sohn, and Blom. These extend existing positioning; preprint-to-publication updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: V6 adds explanatory paragraphs on micro/macro features, FCI steps, and annotation options, plus a sensitivity appendix. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V6 adds Figure 15, standardizes Figure 8's horizontal axes to 0–1 with larger labels, and reduces LIME overlay intensity while retaining the highlighted regions. Publication headers and figure placement also change.

improvement.justification: Appendix C adds useful evidence about dependence on the causal-discovery algorithm, exposing substantial bird-ranking sensitivity. Clearer FCI explanations, explicit finite-sample and annotation-noise limitations, and improved plot readability strengthen the paper modestly. These benefits outweigh the loss of the simulation's stated 0.005 threshold; the core method and original findings remain largely unchanged.
